page.layout: One page of running text in one column, with printed quotation marks (») at the start of each line. No marginal notes. Running head at top centre, page number at top left.

main_text.l: te facere? cui rei, cui gloriæ,
» cui virtuti studere? an juri ci-»
te, cum ædes venderes, ne in »
sellam, in qua tuus sedens pa-»
de Legib. I. his verbis: Ego ve-»

page.notes: The running head is in ornamental capitals and I could not read it letter by letter. The word after "sene-" at the line break is set so that its first letter is unclear; I read it as "ctutisque" with the hyphen joining it to "sene-", and it fits Cicero's "senectutisque", but I have not confirmed it. Long s has been written as plain s throughout. The small marks in the left margin and the dots below the text are stains, not printed text.
